steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13 inch baking pan.

In a large bowl, stir together the oats, flour, brown sugar, salt and baking soda. Cut in the butter to form a crumbly mixture. Reserve 1 1/2 cups of the crumbs, and pat the rest evenly into the bottom of the prepared pan. In a medium bowl, stir together the sweetened condensed milk and peanut butter. Spread evenly over the oatmeal layer. Sprinkle the chocolate chips over the peanut butter layer, then crumble the reserved crust over the top.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes in the preheated oven, until golden brown. Cool completely before cutting into bars.

raw_recipe.headline: Passion Bars
raw_recipe.description: Oatmeal bars with a caramel flavored peanut butter topping.

video.description: Give in to your extreme love of all things chocolate and peanut buttery by baking up these classic bar favorites. Mix oats, flour, brown sugar and butter to create a crumble mixture. Create a crust with some of them, then top with a mixture of peanut butter and sweetened condensed milk. Sprinkle with loads of chocolate chips, and finally top with the last crumbs from your crumble. Bake until golden, cool, cut into bars, and grab one quick before they all disappear!

review.reviewBody: SOOOOOO good! I had half a can of sweetened condensed milk to use up, and I'm so glad I found this recipe! I did a half-batch and I pretty much followed the recipe... Although I didn't measure the peanut butter, just put a huge spoonful of it in the milk. Oh, and a hint: It's much easier to mix the milk/PB-mix and spread it over the crust if you heat it in the microwave for 15 or 30 seconds. Then in blends really easily and it's pretty simple to smooth over the base. I also pressed down on the top crust a little to make sure it would not fall apart. Wonderful! I lined the 8" pan with foil, sprayed it, and it was simple to remove and cut the bars. Thanks, Sue, I LOVE this recipe!

This recipe is very good!!!!! Once you try one, you won't be able to stop eating them!!! I made the recipe as is and it is very good. My advise would be to cut them while they are hot and do not over bake them. I made the mistake of overbaking by an extra 10 minutes as I thought it was not brown enough. Big mistake! I forgot that this are not chewy type of bars. The condensed milk and peanut butter are like hard REALLY hard candy if you over bake them, so cutting them is a challenge once cooled off. My other advice is the type of peanut butter you use. If you use the already sugary brand, you may be able to decrease the brown sugar. If you use the less sugary but creamy, definitely use the full amount of brown sugar the recipe calls for. Also, warm up the peanut butter and condensed milk mixture to make it easier to spread. After keeping these suggestions in mind, you should not be able to stop eating them, guaranteed!

Easy and delicious! Where have you been all my life?! I ate a couple bars, gave my parents a couple bars, and took the rest of the bars to work. Everyone likes them. Predominant flavor is peanut butter, so use good peanut butter. Next flavor is the caramel with an occasional hit of salt. They are sweet, so I cut the bars small. I used regular old fashioned oats. I used dark chocolate chips, which should make the bars a little less sweet, but I think you could use any chocolate chip or chunk chocolate. The chocolate does more to make these look gorgeous than to contribute to flavor. If you have everything in your pantry but the chocolate chips, I say go ahead and make them without! The condensed milk and peanut butter mixture is a little hard to spread, so pour all around as best you can. Someone else commented to warm the mixture slightly (don't cook it!) in the microwave to make spreading easier. I used the tines of a fork to drag it without lifting up the crumb bed. It doesn't spread easily like frosting! This is definitely a good recipe to take to a party or pot luck. It sweet, delicious, and doesn't taste like any other peanut butter or chocolate dessert. Yes, it's a keeper!

I did not have enough chocolate chips so threw in some white chocolate and also butterscotch chips to make the difference. Wow! Big new favorite around here! I liked the bars with the chips I had to use very much but trying all chocolate chips next time. Thanks for the recipe.

Excellent. One of the best baked treats I've ever made. I don't know why, but the peanut butter and condensed milk mixture become caramel. I made this vegan by using soy-free margerine and sweetened condensed coconut milk (does not impart a coconut taste into the dish), as well as Guitard semi-sweet chocolate chips (dairy-free). The only minor change to the recipe I made was to add more chocolate chips, so there was a solid layer.
These were great and super easy. I did heat the condensed milk up as suggested and I probably used more chocolate chips.

Yummy, I did reduce brown sugar as was suggested by 1/3 cup and did not have chocolate chips so I used Hershey bars divided for the chocolate. Excellent! Put in freezer for a few minutes before spreading pb mix, just to make it easier to spread.

This will be a go to can't miss quick and easy everyone will love it...as long as they can eat peanut butter. I use 2 sticks of butter though, placing them in a 9x13 pan, softened in the pre-heating oven just a couple minutes. Meanwhile I mix the dry ingredients in a bowl, and mix the PB and condensed milk in a pirex measure bowl heating them slightly to spread easier. The butter when soft, I put into the dry mix, and follow the rest as written. The butter left in the pan is just a good thing I think. Everyone says yumm!

The are overly sweet. I added bout 3 tbsp more peanut butter to the filling. After baking and cooling they were still not setting up enough to be cut so they need to be refrigerated to set up. I like the mixture of flavors though, so if I make them again I'll cut back on sugar in the crust, add an egg white to hold it together better, and change the filling ratio to more pb and way less sweetened condensed milk.

I did make these with 1 cup of butter to prevent crumbling of the crust. It was very good, but 30 minutes was too long. If I make these again, I will take out after 25 minutes as noted by other reviewers. My oven is right at 350- recently calibrated.

Not the decadent bar I expected from the ingredient list. Overly sweet and crumbly. These satisfy a sweet tooth, but flavor falls flat. Next time I’d reduce the brown sugar and condensed milk by 1/3. Easy to make, filling possibilities are endless.

What I like about these is that the review calls for a lil bit of salt and it tastes like salty sweet! They are chewy. They are so so so delicious! I can’t understand anyone eating these anything less than a five.
Easy and I had everything in my pantry.
These are an absolute must for parties and holidays!!! I always get requests for these at family or holiday functions!!!

Good but very, very sweet. I followed the recipe as directed. Think I'd add a little more salt to the layered ingredients or sprinkle with chopped salted peanuts to offset the sweetness. Gooey goodness throughout. Love the texture of the bars -- especially the edges! -- and the healthy oatmeal addition to the crusty base. Definitely a keeper!
Ooohhh these are awesome and rich! So soft and a bit chewy, and these do NOT get dry and crumbly after the first day, even without refrigeration! Great potluck dessert!
Delicious as-is! Really happy to have come across this recipe!
We love this recipe. I do use Splenda brown sugar and PB2 in place of jar peanut butter for less sugar and calories. The PB2 made the filling less sweet which was perfect for our taste.
No changes made. Great recipe. Delicious. Rich. Will be making these again!
